sop_modules.name: New Drywall Ceiling Preparation
sop_modules.description: Prepare new drywall ceiling surfaces for primer application. Includes inspection and dust removal. NO spot-priming of fasteners — new drywall fasteners are mudded and rust-resistant (RC-001).

tasks.name: Inspect Ceiling Surface
tasks.description: Walk all ceiling surfaces with work light angled to reveal defects: fastener pops, unfilled joints, damaged paper, ridges, or debris. Raking light angle is critical for ceiling inspection — direct overhead light hides defects.

quality_notes.QT2: Note only major defects (fastener pops, holes)
quality_notes.QT3: Identify and mark all visible defects including minor ridges
quality_notes.QT4: Comprehensive inspection under bright raking light, mark all imperfections

tasks.name: Inspect Ceiling Surface (Premium)
tasks.description: Detailed inspection of all ceiling surfaces using work light at raking angle. Mark all imperfections including minor ridges, scratches, and texture inconsistencies. QT4 requires comprehensive defect identification.

quality_notes.QT4: Comprehensive inspection under bright raking light, mark all imperfections for correction

tasks.name: Vacuum Ceiling Drywall Dust
tasks.description: Remove drywall dust from ceiling surfaces using HEPA vacuum with brush attachment. Overhead technique — work systematically. Less dust accumulation on ceilings than walls due to gravity, but still critical for adhesion.

quality_notes.QT2: Quick pass to remove loose dust
quality_notes.QT3: Thorough vacuum of all ceiling surfaces
quality_notes.QT4: Complete vacuum with attention to corners and edges

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Inspect → Vacuum. Inspection identifies issues, vacuum removes dust before priming. NO spot-priming of fasteners — new drywall fasteners are mudded and rust-resistant (RC-001).

sop_modules.name: Floor Protection for Ceiling Spray
sop_modules.description: Set up full-room floor protection before ceiling spray work. Ceiling overspray falls to floor across entire room — full coverage mandatory.

tasks.name: Floor Protection Setup (Full Room)
tasks.description: Install full-room floor protection. Hard floors: rosin paper with taped seams and perimeter tape. Carpet: 1.5 mil plastic with taped edges. Full coverage required — ceiling overspray falls everywhere.

site_condition_rules.affects: Protection material selection: rosin paper for hard floors, plastic for carpet

quality_notes.all: Full room coverage, all seams taped, no gaps

tasks.name: Floor Protection Teardown
tasks.description: Remove floor protection after ceiling priming is complete. Fold toward center to contain debris.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Setup before any spray work. Teardown after all ceiling spray/backroll complete. In NC sequence, floor protection may stay for subsequent wall paint phase.

sop_modules.name: Apply Ceiling Primer - Roller Method
sop_modules.description: Apply primer coat to ceiling using roller with extension pole. Includes cut-in at wall edge.

tasks.name: Cut-In Wall Edge
tasks.description: Brush-cut primer along ceiling-to-wall boundary. Cut line should be clean and extend 2-3 inches onto ceiling for roller overlap. Overhead brush work.

quality_notes.QT4: Crisp edge with minimal brush marks, straight line

tasks.name: Cut-In Wall Edge (Premium)
tasks.description: Premium quality brush-cut primer along ceiling-to-wall boundary. Crisp, straight line with no brush marks. QT4 requires meticulous edge work. Overhead position increases difficulty.

quality_notes.QT4: Crisp edge with minimal brush marks, perfectly straight line

tasks.name: Roll Primer on Ceiling
tasks.description: Apply primer to ceiling field using 9-inch roller on extension pole. Work in one direction, maintain wet edge, avoid lap marks. Overhead work — manage drip risk and roller control.

quality_notes.all: No application defects — no drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks at any quality tier. Surface must be uniformly sealed. (Surface condition imperfections governed by inspection task tolerance.)

tasks.name: Roll Primer on Ceiling (Textured Surface)
tasks.description: Apply primer to textured ceiling surfaces using 3/4-inch nap roller on extension pole. Heavier nap required to work primer into texture valleys. Maintain wet edge. Overhead texture work is slower.

quality_notes.all: No application defects — no drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks at any quality tier. All texture valleys must be filled and sealed.

tasks.name: Roll Primer on Ceiling (Premium)
tasks.description: Premium quality primer application for QT4 finish. Uniform mil thickness, no visible lap marks, consistent sheen across all ceiling surfaces.

quality_notes.all: No application defects — no drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks at any quality tier.
quality_notes.QT4: Additional: verify uniform mil thickness and consistent sheen

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Cut-in first, then roll. Maintain wet edge between cut-in and roll to avoid lap marks.

sop_modules.name: Apply Ceiling Primer - Spray + Backroll Method
sop_modules.description: Apply primer to ceiling via airless spray followed by backroll for consolidation and leveling. Backroll is critical on ceilings — overhead spray alone is prone to runs and uneven coverage.

tasks.name: Mask Adjacent Surfaces for Ceiling Spray
tasks.description: Mask wall tops and any installed fixtures to protect from ceiling overspray. In NC sequence, walls are typically bare — masking wall tops prevents primer from running down wall face.

quality_notes.QT3: Complete masking of wall tops and fixtures
quality_notes.QT4: Precision masking with clean tape lines

tasks.name: Spray Primer on Ceiling
tasks.description: Apply primer via airless sprayer aimed upward. Maintain proper distance, 50% overlap, consistent speed. Work systematically across ceiling. Full PPE required — overspray falls on operator.

quality_notes.all: No application defects — no drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks at any quality tier.

tasks.name: Spray Primer on Ceiling (Premium)
tasks.description: Premium quality ceiling spray primer application. Uniform coverage, consistent mil thickness, no drips or sags. Slower pace with meticulous overlap control.

quality_notes.all: No application defects — no drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks at any quality tier.

tasks.name: Backroll Sprayed Ceiling Primer
tasks.description: Immediately follow spray with 18-inch roller on extension pole to consolidate primer into ceiling surface. Overhead backrolling is significantly more fatiguing than wall backroll. Critical for eliminating air pockets and leveling.

quality_notes.all: No application defects — no drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks at any quality tier. Primer must be fully consolidated into surface.

tasks.name: Backroll Sprayed Ceiling Primer (Premium)
tasks.description: Premium quality ceiling backroll for QT4 finish. Thorough consolidation, no stipple, uniform sheen. Multiple passes if needed. Overhead position limits pass speed.

quality_notes.all: No application defects — no drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks at any quality tier. Primer must be fully consolidated into surface.
quality_notes.QT4: Additional: verify uniform sheen, no stipple

tasks.name: Cut-In Wall Edge After Ceiling Spray
tasks.description: Touch up wall-line edge with brush if needed after spray/backroll. Required if masking line is not crisp or if primer rolled past wall line.

quality_notes.QT3: Clean edge, cover any mask bleed

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Mask → Spray → Backroll (immediately) → Touch-up cut-in. Backroller must follow sprayer closely — spray rate cannot exceed backroll rate.

sop_modules.name: Apply Ceiling Primer - Spray Only Method
sop_modules.description: Apply primer via airless spray without backroll. Less common for ceilings than walls — overhead spray without backroll risks runs and uneven consolidation.

tasks.name: Mask Adjacent Surfaces for Ceiling Spray
tasks.description: Mask wall tops and fixtures to protect from ceiling overspray.

tasks.name: Spray Ceiling Primer (No Backroll)
tasks.description: Apply primer via airless sprayer aimed upward. Higher overlap required when not backrolling to ensure even coverage. Greater drip/run risk on overhead surfaces without backroll.

quality_notes.all: No application defects — no drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks at any quality tier.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Mask → Spray. No backroll means sprayer must achieve final finish in single pass. Higher drip risk on ceilings — slower pace recommended.

sop_modules.name: Ceiling Prime Cleanup
sop_modules.description: Remove masking, clean tools, inspect ceiling prime work.

tasks.name: Remove Masking
tasks.description: Remove all masking tape and paper from wall tops and fixtures. Pull tape at 45-degree angle to avoid peeling primer. NOTE: In NC production sequence, masking may stay in place for subsequent phases — review whether teardown belongs here or in final cleanup spec.

tasks.name: Clean Tools
tasks.description: Clean brushes, rollers, spray equipment with water. Store or dispose properly.

tasks.name: Final Ceiling Inspection
tasks.description: Walk all primed ceiling surfaces. Check for holidays, missed spots, drips, or edge issues. Use raking light for inspection. Touch up as needed.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Remove masking while primer is still slightly tacky for cleanest edge. Clean tools before primer dries.

round_configurations.name: Single Ceiling Prime Round
round_configurations.description: Standard single coat of primer for new drywall ceiling.
round_configurations.notes: Single primer coat is standard for new drywall ceiling with topcoat to follow.

round_configurations.name: Ceiling Prime (Premium)
round_configurations.description: Premium primer application for QT4 ceiling finish.
round_configurations.notes: Light sand of primed surface is prep phase of SF_DRYWALL_CEILING_NC_FINISH, not part of prime spec.
